intro: Here, on the Yeşilırmak, lies Amaseia, an ancient city in Amasya province whose story stretches from the 3rd millennium BC to today. It was the capital of Pontus, it guards royal rock tombs, and it was home to the geographer Strabo. Let us begin.
history: As capital of the Kingdom of Pontus, Amaseia rose under Mithridates VI to become one of the mightiest cities of Anatolia. Its importance did not fade with the kings. Through Roman, Byzantine and Seljuk times it remained a city that mattered, and today its history lies in layers before you: in the rock tombs, in the castle and in the Ottoman mansions.
structure-1: Look up at the cliffs. These are the Pontic Royal Tombs, carved into the rock overlooking the Yeşilırmak valley at Amasya. Here the kings of Pontus chose to rest, high above their capital.
structure-3: Now you come to Aynalı Cave. It is a natural cave, and what makes it special are its rock carvings. Take a moment to look closely.
structure-4: Here are the Yeşilırmak Bridges. Seljuk and Ottoman builders spanned the river at Amasya, and their bridges still tie the two banks together.
structure-5: And now the Ottoman Mansions. These traditional urban houses have survived from the Ottoman period. Imagine the families who once lived behind these walls.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss Amasya Castle, keeping watch over the city.
facts: Did you know? The geographer Strabo was born here in Amaseia. The man who wrote the first comprehensive geography of the known world also described his own town, calling it 'a fortress built by nature'. The rock tombs of the Pontic kings are cut into the cliff above the town, and at night they are lit up. And under the Ottomans, princes learned to govern here as provincial governors, which is why the town is called the 'city of princes'.
outro: This brings our tour of Amaseia to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
